explanation: Two massive bodies (17 and 18) with high G=4.7 start close and fall toward each other, reaching distance ~0.35 at step 23 while velocities spike to ~12. Even with adaptive substeps (13-16 per outer step), the fixed outer dt=0.0176 is too large for this strong, rapidly changing acceleration, causing leapfrog energy drift. Energy rises from E0=-483 to -620 by step 24, exceeding allowed tolerance. Halving dt restores conservation, proving numerical under-resolution of close encounter, not physics.
